transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Patel (Silverline Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Silverline SRE), Priya Singh (Silverline Security)

Summary: quick walkthrough of rate limits, quotas, org/project keys in Redwood Console + API. Went over Hosted vs Dedicated/VPC tradeoffs and security controls (SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps to send pricing, security docs, and schedule benchmark.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood inference. With me is Carlos, our solutions engineer, we'll run through rate limiting and our org/project keys model.
00:14 Dana Patel: Thanks. Quick context, we're replatforming internal LLM endpoints across multiple biz units, want per-tenant quotas and cost isolation, also SSO and audit logs are must-haves. We're exploring hosted first but Dedicated or VPC might be needed.
00:28 Carlos Ruiz: Got it. Today we'll show the Console, API behavior, and the Optimize recommendations that help tune batching + caching to hit cost targets. We'll demo org-level keys and project keys, and how rate-limits can be set at both levels.
00:45 Liam O'Connor: Our peak is around 1k qps per tenant, but most are bursty. Latency targets are 200-300ms for short completions. Cost per token is a big driver obviously.
01:02 Priya Singh: On security: we need SOC2, keys rotation, KMS integration for private deployments, and audit logs tied to user identity via SSO. Also data residency concerns for EU customers.
01:18 Maya Chen: All right, we'll show where those controls live. First, Console quick tour. (background typing noises) You'll see 'Organizations' at top, then projects underneath, each project has its own API key that can be scoped to routes and models.
01:35 Carlos Ruiz: (screen share) Here's a sample org with three projects. For each project we define quota windows, burst sizes, and a per-minute token limit. You can also set per-route limits so the chat route and embedding route are independent.
01:50 Dana Patel: So if Project A hits token cap, will requests fail or queue?
02:00 Carlos Ruiz: Good q. We have configurable behaviors: hard deny (429) or soft-throttle with polled backoffs. For Hosted default we return 429 with a Retry-After header. For Dedicated you can set graceful queueing on the runtime if you enable burst capacity.
02:18 Liam O'Connor: And is that per API key or per org? We need both: global org budget and per-team project budgets.
02:30 Carlos Ruiz: Yep, both. You can set org-level limits to guard spend and project-level to isolate teams. Project keys are tied to projects and optionally tagged with metadata for billing.
02:45 Priya Singh: How about rate limits at route-level — e.g., embeddings are cheap but heavy CPU, want stricter QPS there.
02:58 Carlos Ruiz: You can define per-route token or QPS limits. Also we support model-weighted quotas so models with higher compute count against budget more. Note: small transcription note, sometimes our console label says 'KV cahce' in older builds, ignore that, it's a UI string bug in the demo build.
03:18 Maya Chen: Now API behavior. If you're calling via the Redwood API with a project key header, the runtime enforces project quotas first, then org quotas; there's also leaky-bucket smoothing so short bursts can absorb small spikes.
03:34 Dana Patel: For billing, can we break down token costs by project and by route?
03:45 Carlos Ruiz: Yes — token-level cost breakdowns per key are in the Console billing tab. You can also export per-route token consumption to S3. We showed token breakdown in the Optimize tab where suggestions for batching are tied to cost savings.
04:00 Liam O'Connor: You mentioned prefix caching — how much does that help for chat workloads?
04:12 Carlos Ruiz: For convo flows we do KV cache for prefix tokens which reduces repeat compute. Savings vary; typical reductions are 20-50% depending on reuse. Quantization and batching recommendations from Optimize can further reduce unit cost.
04:28 Dana Patel: For Dedicated / VPC, how different are the rate-limit behaviors?
04:36 Carlos Ruiz: On Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools so backpressure is less likely; you can configure autoscaling policies and define a burst buffer. If you need air-gapped on-prem, rate-control is still enforced locally by the control plane agent. Note: Private deployments can be configured to emit audit logs to your syslog or S3.
04:58 Priya Singh: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys?
05:05 Maya Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, and we can enable BYOK on enterprise contracts.
05:18 Liam O'Connor: Any limits for simultaneous KV cache size or RAM usage?
05:24 Carlos Ruiz: Those are runtime settings per node; for Dedicated we expose config knobs. For hosted we manage those automatically but provide per-tenant quotas so cache memory is partitioned logically.
05:40 Dana Patel: Can you show the Console flow to create org and project keys?
05:46 Carlos Ruiz: Sure. (narration) Click Organizations -> New Org -> name it. Then inside Org click Projects -> New Project -> fill project name, assign owners. On the keys tab you can create a project key and set scopes: read-only, inference-only, or admin. You can also pin the key to a route.
06:10 Dana Patel: Is SSO integrated for the Console?
06:14 Maya Chen: Yes, SSO (SAML/Okta) maps users to roles and those roles map to RBAC permissions in the Console. Audit logs capture who created keys and when.
06:26 Priya Singh: For compliance, do you surface retention settings? We need to show customers how long we keep logs and transcriptions.
06:34 Maya Chen: There's a retention pane. Hosted default is 30 days for transcripts, with add-on retention options. For Private you control retention policies entirely.
06:46 Liam O'Connor: Suppose a single project is noisy — can we throttle it without impacting org?
06:52 Carlos Ruiz: Yes, project-level throttles will cut the project's requests while org-level remains intact. We also support request tagging so you can route critical traffic through higher-priority paths.
07:08 Dana Patel: Could you talk about API keys rotation and secrets management?
07:12 Maya Chen: Keys can be rotated via the Console or the API. We recommend short-lived keys for automation and rotating service tokens. For Dedicated and Private, you can integrate with your secret manager.
07:24 (short silence / typing)
07:30 Carlos Ruiz: Quick demo: I'll create a project key and simulate hitting a per-minute token cap. (sound of clicks) Creating the key... now sending a script of concurrent calls.
07:48 System (Carlos): 00:07 429: rate limit exceeded (Retry-After: 60) — simulated response.
07:55 Liam O'Connor: That Retry-After header is useful, does the SDK auto-handle exponential backoff?
08:02 Carlos Ruiz: Our official SDKs include retry helpers with jitter. For partners or internal SDKs you can implement similar pattern.
08:10 Dana Patel: On billing, is there a soft cap or invoice alert when org-level spend approaches threshold?
08:17 Maya Chen: Yes, you can set alerting thresholds and auto-disable new project keys if spend exceeds org budget. Alerts can be routed to Slack or PagerDuty.
08:30 Priya Singh: Do you support EU data residency for hosted?
08:36 Maya Chen: We have region selection and can pin data to EU regions; for strict residency we recommend a Private deployment.
08:44 Dana Patel: Any notable limitations or gotchas?
08:48 Carlos Ruiz: A few: very small model spawning can increase latency under heavy concurrent requests; choose models and batch sizes accordingly. Also older gen runtimes had a UI label bug (small one we mentioned), and some transcription in our demo recordings swaps Redwood product names — nothing functional but worth calling out.
09:08 Maya Chen: Ok wrapping with next steps: we'll send the pricing and security pack, Carlos will follow up on benchmark plan, and schedule a 1-hour benchmark with Liam and team.
09:18 Dana Patel: Sounds good. Can you include a sample manifest for keys and a template for SSO configs?
09:24 Maya Chen: Yes we'll attach those.
09:28 (meeting closes)

Notes and artifacts referenced: shared deck: https://redwood.example.com/deck/rate-limits-demo, benchmark template: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/template, security pack (to be shared via support portal).

End of transcript.
